Meteorological Department | date = December 2016 | page = M236 | access-date = 21 April 2024}} }} ===Urbanisation=== According to the 2011 census, 79.22% of the population of the Durgapur subdivision was urban and 20.78% was rural. The sole municipal corporation in the Durgapur subdivision is located at [[Durgapur]] and the subdivision has 38 (+1 partly) [[census town]]s (partly presented in the map alongside; all places marked on the map are linked in the full-screen map).{{cite web |url = http://wbpspm.gov.in/publications/District%20Statistical%20Handbook |title = District Statistical Handbook 2014 Burdwan |work = Table 2.2, 2.4(a) |publisher = Department of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of West Bengal |access-date = 15 September 2018 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190121045803/http://www.wbpspm.gov.in/publications/District%20Statistical%20Handbook |archive-date = 21 January 2019 |url-status = dead }} ==Economy== Due to its proximity to the [[Asansol]]-[[Durgapur]] industrial belt, Panagarh has attracted many investments over the years. Emami cements has built a cement grinding plant at Panagarh.{{Cite web| title=Emami cement commissions its panagarh plant in record time of 13 months | url=https://www.emamigroup.com/wp-content/themes/emami/pdf/Emami-Cement-Commissions-its-Panagarh-Plant-23-mar-17.pdf | Force base== [[Panagarh Airport]] was constructed in 1944, during the Second World War. It serves as a base for the Indian Air Force. In 2016, it was renamed as Air Force Station Arjan Singh.{{cite news| url = http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/Panagarh-airbase-renamed-after-former-IAF-chief-Arjan-Singh/article14238800.ece |title = Panagarh airbase renamed after former IAF chief Arjan Singh | work= News, National |date = 15 April 2016 |publisher= The Hindu, 15 April 2016 | access-date = 20 February 2017 }} ==Cantonment== One of the 62 cantonments in the country is located at Panagarh.{{cite web| url = http://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/india/army-fac.htm |title = Indian Army Facilities |publisher= Global Security.org | access-date = 20 February 2017 }} ==Demographics== According to the [[2011 Census of India]], Panagar had a total population of 5,510, of which 2,796 (51%) were males and 2,714 (49%) were females. Population in the age range 0–6 years was 650. The total number of literates in Panagar was 3,836 (78.93% of the population over 6 years).{{cite web| url = http://censusindia.gov.in/pca/pcadata/Houselisting-housing-WB.html |title = 2011 Census – Primary Census Abstract Data Tables | work= West Bengal – District-wise |publisher= Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India | access-date = 20 February 2017 }} ==Transport== [[Panagarh railway station]] is situated on the [[Bardhaman–Asansol section]], which is a part of [[Howrah–Gaya–Delhi line]], [[Howrah–Allahabad–Mumbai line]] and [[Howrah–Delhi main line]].{{cite web| url = http://indiarailinfo.com/train/timetable/barddhaman-asansol-memu-63509/14847/2/7 |title = 63509 Bardhaman-Asansol MEMU |work = Time Table | publisher= India Rail Info | access-date = 9 February 2017}} Earlier, [[National Highway 19 (India)|National Highway 19]] passed through Panagarh Bazar. A bypass was constructed in 2016, avoiding the crowded bazar area. The old [[Grand Trunk Road]] continues to pass through the town.{{cite web| url =https://www.telegraphindia.com/1161211/jsp/bengal/story_124103.jsp#.WK45C_l97IU | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20161211161103/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1161211/jsp/bengal/story_124103.jsp#.WK45C_l97IU | url-status =dead | archive-date =11 December 2016 |title = Political race to open road |work= The Telegraph|date=11 December 2016 | access-date = 20 February 2017 }} [[State Highway 14 (West Bengal)|State Highway 14]] passes through Panagarh. The Dubrajpur–Panagarh sector of SH 14 is part of [[Panagarh–Morgram Highway]].{{cite web| url = http://www.wbtrafficpolice.com/state-highways.php |title = List of State Highways in West Bengal | publisher= West Bengal Traffic Police | access-date = 23 February 2017}}Google Maps ==Education== Panagarh has five primary schools, Rama Krishna Ashrama Vidyapitha, the Kendriya Vidyalaya, Secondary School (Panagarh Railway Colony School) and three higher secondary schools (Panagarh Bazar Hindi High School, Kanksa High School and Kanksa Girls' High School).[https://web.archive.org/web/20070927042719/http://bardhaman.gov.in/education/uschlst.asp?twcd=40901183&twnm=Debipur All India Education Survey 2003]. National Informatics Centre (Burdwan District Unit), Department of Information Technology, Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, India. bardhaman.gov.in, [[File:Panagarh Bazar Hindi High School building.jpg|thumb|Panagarh Bazar Hindi High School building]] ===Professional education=== Panagarh has two engineering colleges viz. Aryabhatta Institute of Engineering & Management Durgapur[http://aiemd.org Welcome to AIEMD: HOME] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120208111141/http://www.aiemd.org/ |date=8 February 2012 }}. Aiemd.org. Retrieved on 2012-03-23. and Techno India, Durgapur. ==Healthcare== Panagarh Rural Hospital, with 30 beds, is the major government medical facility in the Kanksa CD block. There are 4 nonbedded [[Primary Health Centre (India)|primary health centres]] at Malandighi, Shibpur, Shyambazar and Shilampur and 26 health wellness centres.{{cite web | url =https://www.wbhealth.gov.in/other_files/RH.pdf | title =Health & Family Welfare Department | work =Health Statistics – Rural Hospitals | publisher =Government of West Bengal | access-date =12 May 2020 | archive-date =8 October 2022 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20221008143352/https://www.wbhealth.gov.in/other_files/RH.pdf | url-status =dead }}{{cite web | url = https://www.wbhealth.gov.in/other_files/PHC.pdf | title = Health & Family Welfare Department | work = Health Statistics – Primary Health Centres | publisher = Government of West Bengal | access-date = 12 May 2020 | archive-date = 21 April 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180421215645/https://www.wbhealth.gov.in/other_files/PHC.pdf | url-status = dead }} ==References== {{Reflist|3}} {{Paschim Bardhaman District}} [[Category:Cities and towns in Paschim Bardhaman district]] [[Category:Durgapur]]
extract: Panagarh is an industrial neighborhood and an Indian Air Force base in the Durgapur city of the Paschim Bardhaman district in the Indian state of West Bengal.
